provenance.event: A coordinated cyber attack causing DDoS-like network congestion, targeted dependency outages, resource exhaustion, and a container crash during a peak-hour flash promotion across all three demo storefronts.
provenance.thought: The steady states require response contracts, latency within timeouts, and availability at declared replica counts. The main weaknesses likely are single-replica critical services, no circuit breakers/retries on payment dependencies, and insufficient CPU resource limits. I first kill a product catalog pod to expose recovery/redundancy weakness; if only one replica exists, the frontend loses catalog data. Next I inject total packet loss on payment in both checkout systems to reveal missing fallback/retry and immediate contract violation. Then I stress CPU on the station service to expose resource allocation deficiency, causing cascading latency. After that, I apply sustained 2s latency on station, order, checkout, and payment edges to saturate timeouts and connection pools. Finally I drop email traffic to verify whether a non-critical dependency can fail without breaking the main checkout contract. This order simulates an attack wave: initial crash, total dependency loss, resource exhaustion, sustained latency, and partial outage.
